4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	## Clarifications
10	
11	### Session 2026-10-24
12	
13	- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
14	
15	**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
16	
17	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
18	
19	### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)
20	
21	From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.
22	
23	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.
24	
25	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
30	2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
31	3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
32	4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.
33	
34	---
35	
36	### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)
37	
38	Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.
39	
40	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.
41	
42	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.
43	
44	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
45	
46	1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
47	2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
48	3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).
49	
50	---
51	
52	### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)
53	
54	The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.
55	
56	**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.
57	
58	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.
59	
60	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
61	
62	1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
63	2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.
64	
65	---
66	
67	### Edge Cases
68	
69	- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
70	- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
71	- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
72	- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
73	- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.
74	- Opening My Records itself, its filters, its tags, the chat, the dashboard, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
75	
76	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
77	
78	### Functional Requirements
79	
80	- **FR-001**: A download icon in My Records' header MUST open the export bottom sheet.
81	- **FR-002**: Opening the export sheet MUST request an export for the period currently represented by My Records' active date filter (or the full history if no date filter is applied), including the narrative by default.
82	- **FR-003**: If the requested period contains zero entries, the sheet MUST show the "Período vazio" state immediately — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — with no download control offered and no job left running.
83	- **FR-004**: For a period with at least one entry, the sheet MUST show "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...") immediately after the request, then transition to "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) while the job is still working toward a result, without requiring any user action to advance between these states.
84	- **FR-005**: When the job's data and narrative both complete successfully, the sheet MUST show "Concluído" with two enabled controls — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
85	- **FR-006**: When the job's data completes but the narrative generation fails or is skipped, the sheet MUST show "Erro" with text explaining that the AI summary failed while the data remains available, and exactly one enabled control — "Baixar dados brutos" — with no PDF option offered.
86	- **FR-007**: When the job fails entirely (no data produced, not only the narrative), the sheet MUST show a failure state with a generic message explaining the export itself could not be generated — text distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation, shown the same way regardless of the backend's specific error code — no download control at all, and only the "Fechar" link available (no dedicated in-sheet retry control; retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again, per FR-011). This state MUST be visually and functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure.
87	- **FR-008**: "Baixar PDF" MUST only ever be offered when FR-005's conditions hold, and tapping it MUST download a PDF containing the generated narrative for the exported period.
88	- **FR-009**: "Baixar dados brutos" MUST be offered in both the FR-005 and FR-006 outcomes, and tapping it MUST download the user's raw entry data for the exported period, independent of whether the narrative ever succeeded.
89	- **FR-010**: A "Fechar" link MUST be present and functional in every one of the six sheet states ("Pendente", "Processando", "Concluído", "Erro" [FR-006's narrative-only failure], the full-failure state [FR-007], and "Período vazio"), dismissing the sheet without cancelling any in-flight backend job and without affecting My Records' own list, filters, or scroll position.
90	- **FR-011**: Repeated taps on the download icon, or on a download button that already has a request in flight, MUST NOT create multiple concurrent export jobs or fire duplicate download requests for the same action.
91	- **FR-012**: If the session expires while the export sheet is open, the existing session-expiration handling (RF07) MUST take over exactly as it does elsewhere on the screen, and the sheet MUST resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated rather than remaining stuck.
92	- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT implement manual-tag or category filtering, or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2); MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF05 in the build order; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
93	
94	### Key Entities
95	
96	- **Export Job**: An ephemeral, user-scoped job created by one export request, covering one period of entries. Carries an overall status (preparing / generating / data-ready-without-narrative / fully done / failed) and a narrative status that advances independently of it (pending / generating / done / failed / skipped), since the raw data and the AI narrative can finish — or fail — on different timelines. Produces, at most, two downloadable artifacts (a PDF narrative and the raw data) once it reaches a state where either is available. It is not a journal entry and is never shown anywhere outside the export sheet.
97	
98	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
99	
100	### Measurable Outcomes
101	
102	- **SC-001**: A user exporting a period that has at least one entry can reach a downloaded, readable narrative PDF end-to-end, with zero crashes and zero empty or malformed files, across all tested periods.
103	- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.
104	- **SC-003**: Exporting a period with zero entries is communicated through a single, clear sheet state in 100% of tested cases, with zero downloadable files ever produced and zero crashes.
105	- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
106	- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.
107	
108	## Assumptions
109	
110	- **Period selection**: The export sheet exports whatever period My Records' own active date filter currently represents (or the entire history, if no date filter is applied) rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself — the prototype's export sheet shows no period-selection control of its own, and My Records already owns date filtering (RF06/RF07).
111	- **Narrative inclusion**: Every export request includes the narrative by default (there is no prototype control to opt out of it upfront) — a request only ends up "without narrative" when generation fails or is skipped, never by the user's deliberate choice.
112	- **When downloads become available**: The two download buttons appear only once the job reaches one of the sheet's defined terminal states — "Concluído" or "Erro" — matching the prototype's literal five-state catalog. The backend can report an intermediate state where the raw data is ready but the narrative is still generating; this unit treats that intermediate state as still part of "Processando" visually (no early download link appears mid-generation), since the prototype defines no sixth state for it and the acceptance criteria ("the export is not blocked by an AI failure") are fully satisfied once "Erro" exposes the raw-data download — nothing in the source material requires exposing it earlier than that.
113	- **Full job failure vs. narrative-only failure**: These are treated as two distinct outcomes (see FR-006 vs. FR-007) because the backend distinguishes them (an overall failed job produces no data at all, so there is nothing to download) — the prototype's single "Erro" state is understood to describe the narrative-only failure specifically, since its own text says the data remains available.
114	- **Resuming an export after leaving the sheet**: Closing "Fechar" does not cancel the underlying job, but this unit does not add a job-history or notification feature for jobs left running in the background — the prototype has no such affordance. Reopening the export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job.
115	- **File handling on download**: "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" trigger the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a downloaded file; this unit is not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer.
116	- **Status polling**: The exact interval at which the sheet checks `GET /export/:jobId/status` while "Pendente"/"Processando" is an implementation detail, not a product requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck.

- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases (for a period with entries), the user still completes a raw-data download from the same sheet, with a clear explanation of what happened.
- **SC-003**: Exporting a period with zero entries is communicated through a single, clear sheet state in 100% of tested cases, with zero downloadable files ever produced and zero crashes.
- **SC-004**: Closing the export sheet, from any of its five states, leaves My Records' list, active filters, and scroll position completely unchanged in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-005**: No export attempt — successful, narrative-failed, fully failed, or empty-period — ever leaves the sheet showing a "preparing" or "generating" indicator indefinitely; every attempt reaches one of its defined terminal states within the system's normal response time.

## Assumptions

- **Period selection**: The export sheet exports whatever period My Records' own active date filter currently represents (or the entire history, if no date filter is applied) rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself — the prototype's export sheet shows no period-selection control of its own, and My Records already owns date filtering (RF06/RF07).
- **Narrative inclusion**: Every export request includes the narrative by default (there is no prototype control to opt out of it upfront) — a request only ends up "without narrative" when generation fails or is skipped, never by the user's deliberate choice.
- **When downloads become available**: The two download buttons appear only once the job reaches one of the sheet's defined terminal states — "Concluído" or "Erro" — matching the prototype's literal five-state catalog. The backend can report an intermediate state where the raw data is ready but the narrative is still generating; this unit treats that intermediate state as still part of "Processando" visually (no early download link appears mid-generation), since the prototype defines no sixth state for it and the acceptance criteria ("the export is not blocked by an AI failure") are fully satisfied once "Erro" exposes the raw-data download — nothing in the source material requires exposing it earlier than that.
- **Full job failure vs. narrative-only failure**: These are treated as two distinct outcomes (see FR-006 vs. FR-007) because the backend distinguishes them (an overall failed job produces no data at all, so there is nothing to download) — the prototype's single "Erro" state is understood to describe the narrative-only failure specifically, since its own text says the data remains available.
- **Resuming an export after leaving the sheet**: Closing "Fechar" does not cancel the underlying job, but this unit does not add a job-history or notification feature for jobs left running in the background — the prototype has no such affordance. Reopening the export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job.
- **File handling on download**: "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" trigger the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a downloaded file; this unit is not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer.
- **Status polling**: The exact interval at which the sheet checks `GET /export/:jobId/status` while "Pendente"/"Processando" is an implementation detail, not a product requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck.

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `api/openapi.yaml` | API contract of the 23 endpoints — the source of truth |
| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |
| `export-screen-states.md` | Mapping between the export screen states and the export job statuses (RF05) |
| `sync-badge.md` | Semantics of the per-entry synchronization badge |
| `known-bugs.md` | Known non-blocking backend defects, with workarounds |
| `fixtures/` | Test media (audio, images for OCR), the expected transcription of the audio, and the three seeded entries used by semantic search |

Credentials (project URL and keys) are not in this package: they are provided in the app's `.env`.

## Contract path → function

`api/openapi.yaml` has no router: each operation is served by its own Edge Function at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` (see `servers` and each operation's `x-cerne-function` in the YAML) — **never** directly at the REST path below. Path parameters are appended as the final URL segments, in the same order as they appear in the path; any literal segment after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in the real URL.

content.content:
9:**Input**: User description: "P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault: Protect access to the user's data with a Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier, validated on the device, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF03) and section 10 (parameters), matching the prototype states 'Tela 0.1 — Biometria', 'Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial', 'Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha'. No biometric endpoint exists on the backend; the biometrics preference is stored via PATCH /account/settings, and the session is renewed with POST /auth/refresh or POST /auth/login after passing the barrier. Depends on F000 (session, login). Do not implement features of later units, extension features, or change the backend."
15:- Q: During first-time PIN setup, if the user opts into Face ID/Touch ID and the `PATCH /account/settings` call to save `biometricEnabled` fails (timeout, no connection, etc.), should that block the user from reaching Home/Chat, or should the app proceed locally and let the write resolve/retry in the background? → A: Proceed locally and retry in the background — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already work regardless of backend reachability; first-time setup does not block on this write succeeding, consistent with the local-first philosophy of FR-002 and FR-015 (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
91:- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.
99:- **FR-003**: When biometrics are enabled and available on the device, the system MUST attempt Face ID/Touch ID first; when biometrics are unavailable (no hardware, nothing enrolled, or disabled), the system MUST present PIN entry as the method shown, without attempting a biometric prompt.
109:- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
110:- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
120:- **Biometrics Preference**: An account-level flag (`biometricEnabled`) indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's enrolled unlock method; read and written through the backend's account-settings endpoint, but never the thing that performs the actual biometric check.
135:- A dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later (outside of first-time setup) belongs to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit; this unit implements the account-settings read/write path for `biometricEnabled` but not that screen's UI.
141:- The Face ID/Touch ID prompt is triggered automatically as soon as the vault screen with biometrics enabled appears (standard platform behavior), not only after a tap; the fingerprint circle and "Toque para desbloquear" act as a manual retry affordance for when the OS prompt was dismissed or cancelled, consistent with User Story 1's requirement that the prompt appear before any data is shown on cold launch.
142:- When a user disables biometrics at the OS level between sessions (see Edge Cases), this unit does not call the backend to flip `biometricEnabled` to false; the account-level preference is only ever written during first-time setup (FR-013) in this unit, and keeping it in sync with later out-of-band OS changes is left to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit, consistent with the existing assumption that a dedicated toggle belongs there.

content.content:
## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |
| Audio waveform | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | active/animated (recording) · frozen and faded (processing) |
| Skeleton | Any content loaded over the network | shown for calls longer than 300 ms (RNF01) |

# Feature Specification: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)

The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.

---

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.

---

### Edge Cases

- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle is not offered, or is shown disabled, rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.

Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. ## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)

The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.

---

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).

Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)

The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.

---

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.

---

### Edge Cases

- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle is not offered, or is shown disabled, rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.
- **FR-003**: When the aggregate for the active period contains zero entries, the dashboard MUST show the light-gray placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
- **FR-004**: When the aggregate contains exactly one entry, the dashboard MUST show a single small bar and "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
- **FR-005**: When the aggregate contains enough entries to populate the chart's full bucket set (the "more than thirty entries" scenario), the dashboard MUST render the multi-bar chart from the aggregate data and MUST request the narrative, showing it once it resolves.
- **FR-006**: If the narrative call fails, times out, or returns an error after the chart has already rendered successfully, the dashboard MUST show a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message in the narrative's place, without affecting the already-rendered chart and without being confused with the zero-entries empty state.
- **FR-007**: If the aggregate call itself fails, the dashboard MUST show a clear, non-crashing, retryable error state for the chart area, distinct from the zero-entries state, and MUST NOT request the narrative until the aggregate succeeds.
- **FR-008**: The dashboard MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened, never served from a result cached from a previous visit, so that an entry created elsewhere is reflected the next time Settings is opened.
- **FR-009**: Settings MUST display the account's initials avatar, current display name, and current email (read-only) — email MUST NOT be editable in this unit, since `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no email field and rejects attempts to change it.
- **FR-010**: Settings MUST let the user edit their display name through an inline pencil-to-check control; saving MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `displayName` (1–80 characters) and MUST update the locally displayed/cached name on success.
- **FR-011**: A client-side validation MUST block submitting an empty name or one longer than 80 characters, with no backend call made and the field left in edit mode with an inline error.
- **FR-012**: If the name save fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the field MUST remain in edit mode with the user's typed value intact, show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT silently revert or discard the typed text.
- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, Settings MUST offer a toggle reflecting the account's current `biometricEnabled` preference and MUST let the user change it; changing it MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `biometricEnabled` value, continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established for this same flag. On a device with no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled, the toggle MUST NOT be offered as actionable.
- **FR-014**: If the biometric toggle save fails, the toggle MUST revert to its last-confirmed state and show a clear, retryable error, rather than appearing to succeed.
- **FR-015**: This unit MUST NOT build the AI persona selector ("Analítico"/"Empático"/"Socrático") or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2), even though `PATCH /account/settings` also carries a `persona` field for that extension.
- **FR-016**: Settings MUST offer a "Sair" action that calls `POST /auth/logout` and, regardless of whether that call succeeds or fails, MUST clear the local session and any cached account/profile state and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no dedicated "signed out" success screen.
- **FR-017**: Settings MUST offer an "Apagar conta" action (styled as destructive/red) that opens a confirmation dialog matching the prototype — red title "Apagar sua conta?", text stating the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button — and MUST NOT call the delete endpoint before this dialog is explicitly confirmed.
- **FR-018**: Confirming the dialog MUST call `DELETE /account` with the backend-required `confirmation: "DELETE"` value supplied by the app itself (the user is not asked to type the word "DELETE"; the dialog's own destructive button tap is the explicit confirmation, matching the prototype's two-button dialog with no text field).
- **FR-019**: On a successful account deletion, the app MUST clear all local session, cached account/profile, and any other locally held user data, and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own — mirroring FR-016's logout behavior.
- **FR-020**: If the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the account MUST remain intact, the dialog MUST show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT report success.
- **FR-021**: Cancelling the delete-confirmation dialog MUST dismiss it without any backend call and without altering any Settings state (dashboard, profile fields, or toggle values).
- **FR-022**: Repeated taps on "Sair" or "Apagar tudo" before a prior request for the same action resolves MUST NOT fire a second concurrent request.
- **FR-023**: If the session expires while Settings is open, the existing expired-session handling (F000, continued by RF07) MUST take over exactly as elsewhere, and re-authenticating MUST return the user to a Settings screen that re-requests the dashboard and profile data rather than showing stale or broken state.
- **FR-024**: This unit MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF09 in the build order; MUST NOT implement any extension feature (requirements, section 2) beyond what FR-015 already excludes; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Dashboard Aggregate**: The chart data for one period — a set of date-bucketed counts (split by entry source: manual/audio/photo/chat) plus totals. Always returns a well-formed (possibly all-zero) result rather than an error for an account with no entries; recomputed fresh on every Settings visit, never persisted locally across visits.
- **Dashboard Narrative**: An independently-fetched, AI-generated paragraph describing the aggregate's pattern for the same period. Can succeed, fail, or be skipped (zero/one-entry scenarios) independently of whether the aggregate itself loaded successfully.
- **Account Profile**: The user's editable identity on this screen — display name (editable), email (read-only), and the biometric-unlock preference (editable, shared with RF03). Since the backend only ever returns this profile as the response of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call — there is no endpoint to read it standalone — the app treats the most recent successful write (from this unit or from RF03's first-time setup) as the locally held source of truth for what this screen displays, defaulting sensibly (e.g., name derived from email) for an account that has never had a successful write.
- **Account Deletion**: A one-way, irreversible action with no corresponding entity afterward — it ends the account and every row tied to it (RNF05), including the signed-in session itself.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Across accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries, the dashboard renders the correct dedicated state in 100% of cases with zero crashes and zero mixed-up states (e.g., the empty-history message never appears alongside chart data).
- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases where the chart data itself loaded successfully, the chart remains fully visible and correct, with a distinct, clear explanation shown only in the narrative's place.
- **SC-003**: 100% of confirmed account-deletion attempts that succeed on the backend leave the device with no retained local session, cached profile, or other user data, and no path back into the account without creating a new one.
- **SC-004**: Zero account deletions occur without the user explicitly reaching and confirming the destructive dialog — cancelling or dismissing it never results in a deleted account.
- **SC-005**: A display-name edit that succeeds is still showing the new value after the app is fully restarted, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-006**: Signing out, from any state the screen can be in, always results in the user reaching the authentication entry point with no residual access, in 100% of tested cases.

## Assumptions

- **Dashboard period**: The dashboard requests a single, fixed period rather than exposing a period-switching control, since neither the prototype's four Settings states nor its component library describes any period selector, tab, or chip for this screen — only the entry-count-driven states (zero / one / more-than-thirty) are depicted. The backend's `period` enum (`7d`/`30d`/`90d`/`all`) exists independently of this UI decision; this unit sends one fixed value (`all`, so the "more than thirty entries" scenario and the cache-invalidation acceptance criterion are both naturally satisfiable from the user's full history) and does not expose the other three values as a feature of this unit.
- **No endpoint to read the current profile**: `GET /auth/session` returns only `id` and `email`; the only way to learn `displayName`, `persona`, or `biometricEnabled` is the response body of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call. This unit treats the most recent such response (including ones written by RF03's first-time biometric setup) as the locally cached source of truth for what Settings displays, with a sensible default (e.g., a name derived from the email's local part) for an account whose profile has never been successfully written.
- **Email is read-only despite the prototype's pencil icon**: The prototype extract describes "editable name/e-mail" with a shared pencil-to-check control, but the frozen API contract's `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no `email` field and explicitly rejects email changes. Per the requirements document's own rule ("where this differs from the API contract, the contract prevails"), this unit treats only the display name as editable and shows the email as plain, read-only text.
- **No typed "DELETE" confirmation text field**: The backend requires the literal request field `confirmation: "DELETE"`, but the prototype's confirmation dialog shows only a title, explanatory text, and two buttons — no text input. This unit treats the destructive button tap itself as the required explicit confirmation and supplies the literal value in the request automatically, without asking the user to type anything.
- **Where "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" land**: The prototype extract states both actions return to the "Biometria" screen with no dedicated success screen of their own. Since both actions end with no stored session, and F000 already routes a device with no stored session to the login/sign-up screen on next launch, this unit treats "the app's authentication entry point" as whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a separate destination.
- **Biometric toggle is in scope, persona is not**: RF03's own specification explicitly defers the biometric on/off toggle (outside of first-time setup) to "the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit." The persona selector, by contrast, is explicitly listed as a non-implemented extension feature (requirements, section 2) even though both preferences share the same `PATCH /account/settings` endpoint.
- **Chart's fixed bucket count**: The "more than thirty entries" scenario is rendered using the aggregate's date buckets mapped onto the prototype's fixed-size bar chart (ten bars in the reference mock); this unit does not need to support an arbitrary, unbounded number of visible bars.
